Package hadur117.sepia

Class InkPlanner

java.lang.Object
hadur117.sepia.InkPlanner
public final class InkPlanner extends Object
The ink planner (INK-1 to INK-5): where to aim a 0.1 bullet so that it stops the most danger over the landings Sepia has fixed.

The engine destroys two bullets whose segments of the same turn cross. A bullet of the enemy's wave flies on a ray from the wave's source, so to stop the bullets aimed at a bearing in the hit set, our bullet must cross that bearing inside the ring the wave sweeps on the same turn. The planner solves for those crossings rather than sweeping every angle: for each wave, at the hit set's middle and both edges, it finds the turn on which our bullet can be where that bearing's bullet is, and aims there (INK-3). Each candidate is then scored with the kernel's BulletShadows over every wave in flight: the share of each hit set it newly shades, walked up to the turn the wave can meet the body (INK-5), with each newly shaded bearing weighed by the chance that wave's bullet is on it, and by its damage (INK-1).

Stateless apart from its inputs; each call builds its candidates afresh.

  • Method Details

    • best

      public InkPlanner.Shot best(List<InkWave> waves, long fireTime, Point2D.Double from, double gunHeading, double maxGunTurn, AimBelief belief)
      The best ink aim for a shot leaving from on tick fireTime, or null when no candidate shades anything.
      Parameters:
      waves - the waves to shade; each must have its landing fixed and its shadows current
      fireTime - the tick the shot would leave on
      from - where Sepia would stand that tick
      gunHeading - the gun's heading now, radians
      maxGunTurn - how far the gun can turn before fireTime, radians
      belief - where the enemy aims
      Returns:
      the best shot, or null

    • score

      InkPlanner.Shot score(List<InkWave> live, AimBelief belief, long fireTime, Point2D.Double from, double aim)
      Scores one aim over live: the share of each hit set it shades that the bullets in the air do not, walked up to the turn the wave meets the body. What it is worth weighs each newly shaded bearing by the aim belief, so shade on the bearings the enemy is likely to use counts for more than shade on its unlikely edge.

    • candidates

      List<Double> candidates(List<InkWave> live, long fireTime, Point2D.Double from)
      INK-3: the candidate aims, at most MAX_CANDIDATES, nearest wave first. For each wave and each of three bearings in its hit set, the aim that puts our bullet on that bearing's bullet on the turn the two can first share a ring, and on the turn after.

    • meet

      static List<Double> meet(InkWave w, double bearing, long fireTime, Point2D.Double from, double speed)
      The aims that put a bullet of speed, leaving from on fireTime, where the wave's bullet on bearing is: at the turn the two first meet, solved between whole turns, and half a turn later. Empty when our bullet cannot reach that bullet before the wave meets the body.
